## feature

<!-- new capability this task added -->

### read-base split columns in error.parquet

```
level: high
```

#### reason

A unit test reads the written Parquet and asserts the nine-column schema and the `to_c` value, and the full suite and lint pass this session.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The `--error-out` file (`{p}.error.parquet`) now writes nine columns: `seq_name`, `position`, `insertion`, `deletion`, `mismatch`, `to_a`, `to_c`, `to_g`, `to_t`.
2. `to_x` counts the in-region substitutions at that 1-based position whose read (destination) base is x.
3. The tally increments the four counters inside the existing `*` branch, so the change adds no extra pass over the BAM.

#### before

Each position carried one `mismatch` total. A user could not tell which base the reads carried at a failing position without a separate per-base analysis.

#### after

Each position's mismatch count is split by destination base in the same file. Position-level error plots can now show the substitution direction.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:31-34` — new `to_a/to_c/to_g/to_t` fields on `_PositionalErrorCounts`.
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:222-229` — destination-base increments in the `*` branch.
- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:316-319` — the four counts passed to the writer.
- `src/sam_tagger/parquet_writer.py:67-113` — 9-column `PositionalErrorStats` schema, all new columns `UInt64`.
- `tests/test_stats.py:212` — `test_error_stats_write_all_seven` asserts the schema and the `to_c=1` row at position 21.

:::

## fix

None

## limitation

### no to_n column

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The user explicitly chose the 4-column option over the 5-column option with `to_n`, and the code increments `to_*` only for read-base index 0–3.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. A substitution whose read base is N counts in `mismatch` and in no `to_*` column.
2. Adding `to_n` later is one more field, one more branch arm, and one more column.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py:220-229` — the comment records that read-base N (idx 4) has no column.

:::

## caveat

### to_* sum can be below mismatch

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The condition is structural (N has no column), a test pins both N cases, and the semantics are written into the user docs.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Do not assert `to_a + to_c + to_g + to_t == mismatch` on real data.
2. Read-base-N substitutions and ref-N/read-ACGT substitutions both widen the gap: ref-N events land in `to_*`, read-N events do not.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `tests/test_stats.py:162` — `test_error_stats_tally_mismatch_n_read_base`: `*an` gives mismatch 1 with all `to_*` 0, `*na` gives `to_a` 1.
- `docs/usage.qmd:163-166` — the semantics note under the outputs table.

:::

## assumption

### to_* counts the read base as the destination

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

I inferred the direction from the name `to_*` and stated it in the option the user selected. The user accepted the option but never confirmed the direction in their own words.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The implementation reads `to_x` as "the read moved to base x at this position".
2. If the intended meaning was the reference base instead, the columns answer the mirrored question.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `docs/usage.qmd:163-164` — the shipped wording: "splits each position's `mismatch` count by the read (destination) base".

:::

## conclusion

### error.parquet carries a per-position destination-base split

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The schema and values are verified by a test that reads the written Parquet file, and the full suite passes.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The wider schema is additive, so column-name-based readers keep working.
2. The cost matches the feasibility estimate: four integer increments per substitution event and a small memory and file-size increase.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `pixi run -e dev test` → `133 passed in 1.36s` (2 new/extended test bodies included).
- `pixi run -e dev lint` → `All checks passed!`

:::

## recommendation

### L: notify error.parquet consumers of the wider schema

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The schema change is additive but visible, and any strict-schema consumer breaks on the new columns. I have not audited who those consumers are.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Tell downstream users of `error.parquet` about the four new columns before they upgrade.
2. Name-based column selection and `pl.read_parquet` are unaffected.
